To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The heat capacity of thick desert leaves can prevent excursions into the damaging high temperatures that can occur during lulls in air movements.

small increases in leaf size can prevent excursions into damaging high temperatures during periods of low wind speed, and this effect is greatest when other mechanisms for reducing leaf temperature are lacking.

(1) small increases in leaf size (0.1-0.5 mm thick) could reduce leaf temperature and prevent excursions into lethal temperatures during transient low wind speed events; (2) the benefit of increased thickness is greatest for leaves with low rates of transpiration and low reflectance (low transpirative cooling); (3) the benefit of thickness is greater for small leaves (less transpirative cooling).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal ecology of desert plants and the role of leaf thickness in preventing thermal stress during transient lulls in air flow.
the thermal ecology of leaves in a desert environment, and the effect of leaf thickness on the avoidance of damage by high temperatures.
the role of leaf thickness in reducing the incidence of thermal damage to leaves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leaf thickness is a critical factor in determining leaf thermal damage during low wind speeds, especially in the case of leaves that have a low capacity for transpirational cooling.
leaf thickness is important, in addition to other factors, in reducing the risk of thermal damage during low wind speeds.
leaf thickness can play a major role in avoiding thermal damage during low wind speeds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leaf thickness is a key determinant for the thermal response of desert plants.
the thickness of leaves in desert plants is an important adaptation to the risk of extreme heat stress, which is a significant threat to their survival.
thick leaves are not just a consequence of low wind speed, but are a mechanism for coping with low wind speeds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even a small increase in leaf thickness can reduce the incidence of extreme thermal stress.
small increases in thickness can reduce thermal stress, and thus may be important in the evolution of leaf thickness.
small increases in leaf size can have a large effect on leaf temperature and thermal damage avoidance.
